sub_answers.sub_question: What documented instances of participant shortages, event cancellations, or category omissions have occurred at Latvian championships?
What governance disputes or controversies (selection, judging, federation decisions) have been reported in Latvian figure skating history?
How have resource limitations (rinks, funding, coaching availability) impacted staging or competitiveness of Latvian national championships?
sub_answers.text: Latvia has lacked a primary national stadium for many years, causing the national team to play in stadiums that do not meet UEFA/FIFA standards due to low seating capacity [d17125690s7p0]. Plans to build a modern 15,000–20,000 seat stadium were put on hold because of unclear funding strategies among investors and governing bodies [d17125690s7p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Have there been criticisms or external assessments about the competitiveness or international relevance of Latvia's national championships?
sub_answers.text: Existing major stadiums in Riga (Daugava and Skonto) do not meet UEFA/FIFA standards because they have seating capacities under 11,000, which has been highlighted as a limitation [d17125690s7p0]. The need for a modern, multi-use stadium has been publicly discussed as important for hosting international events and improving Latvia's football profile [d17125690s7p0].
